title: Badrinath Temple: Darshan Timings, Story, Dates & How to Reach
seo_title: Badrinath Temple: Timings, Story, Dates & How to Reach
seo_desc: Badrinath temple guide: the legend of Badri Vishal, darshan timings, 2026 and 2027 dates, free registration, altitude and the road from Rishikesh.
label: Badrinath Dham
sub: Shri Badrinath Dham is the shrine of Vishnu as Badrinarayan, the last of Uttarakhand's Char Dham and one of the four dhams of India. The legend of the badri tree, darshan timings, opening and closing dates, free registration and the road from Rishikesh — no trek needed.
q: Where is Badrinath temple and why is it sacred?
answer: Badrinath temple stands at about 3,100 m on the Alaknanda river in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, between the Nar and Narayan ranges. It is the shrine of Vishnu as Badrinarayan — one of the four dhams of India, one of the 108 Divya Desams and the last stop of the Char Dham Yatra. A road reaches the town, so there is no trek.
intro: For many families Badrinath is the gentlest of the Himalayan dhams: the road climbs all the way to the town, and the temple is a short walk across the Alaknanda bridge. Its bright painted façade faces the river, with the Neelkanth peak behind and the Nar and Narayan ranges on either side. The Badrinath Mandir is managed by the Shri Badarinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC).

The deity is a small black Shaligram stone image of Vishnu seated in meditation, flanked in the sanctum by Kuber, Narada, Uddhava and Nar–Narayan; Lakshmi has her own shrine in the complex. By a long custom the chief priest, the Rawal, is a Nambudiri Brahmin from Kerala — a living link between the Himalaya and the far south. Badrinath is a Vishnu shrine, not a Jyotirlinga; its Shiva neighbour on the yatra is Kedarnath.

story.lead: The Puranas and local tradition tell why Vishnu chose this cold valley. This is how it is told.
beats: It is believed that Vishnu once sat in deep meditation here, in the bitter Himalayan cold, unmoved by snow and sun.
To shield him, Lakshmi stood over him in the form of a badri (jujube) tree, through every storm.
Moved by her devotion, Vishnu named the place Badrikashram and took the name Badri-Nath, the Lord of the Badri.
Tradition also places the long penance of the sages Nar and Narayan here — which is why the two ranges carry their names.
more: A popular telling adds that this valley was once the home of Shiva and Parvati, until Vishnu came as a crying infant, was sheltered by Parvati, and then claimed the spot for his meditation — so Shiva moved on to Kedarnath. Not every Purana has this tale; it is told as tradition, not history.

extra_sections.label: History
extra_sections.h2: A short history of Badrinath temple
extra_sections.html:
Adi Shankaracharya is credited with reviving Badrinath as a centre of worship (traditions differ on the century). Garhwal kings moved the image to the present temple in the 16th century and expanded it in the 17th. The custom of a Nambudiri Rawal from Kerala is said to date from 1776.

The 1803 Garhwal earthquake badly damaged the temple; it was rebuilt largely with help from the King of Jaipur. In 2026 the temple drew a record 18.10 lakh+ pilgrims by 29 September (DD India).

darshan.note: Phones and photography inside the sanctum: follow the temple staff's instructions. Queues can be long in May–June.

route.h2: The road from Rishikesh to Badrinath
route.lead: Badrinath is a drive-up dham: the highway follows the Ganga and then the Alaknanda past the five prayags. About 298 km in all; distances are approximate.
stops: Railhead, registration counters and the start of the mountain road.
Where the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi meet to become the Ganga.
The Kedarnath road turns off up the Mandakini; Badrinath traffic stays on the Alaknanda.
Two more confluences; Adi Badri lies about 17 km from Karnaprayag.
Narsingh temple, Badrinath's winter seat; Auli is close by.
Past Pandukeshwar to the town; a short walk across the bridge to the temple.
route.note: The highway is landslide-prone in the monsoon, especially around Jyotirmath — keep a buffer day and check road status before you set off.

cards: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, is the nearest — about 315 km by road.
Yog Nagari Rishikesh station is the nearest railhead; Haridwar has more trains.
Rishikesh → Devprayag → Rudraprayag → Karnaprayag → Jyotirmath → Badrinath, about 298 km. Buses, shared taxis and cars run in season; a Rishikesh taxi can be booked for the whole run.
There is no IRCTC HeliYatra service for Badrinath. Private charters from Dehradun exist — verify the operator yourself and never pay "seat sellers" on WhatsApp.

items: Char Dham registration is compulsory and free on registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in, the Tourist Care Uttarakhand app or helpline 1364. Any site charging a "registration fee" is fake.
The road reaches the town and the temple is a short walk away. The altitude still matters: Uttarakhand advises a check-up for anyone over 50 or with heart, lung or blood-pressure conditions.
May–June and September–October. July–August brings landslides on the highway, though the temple stays open.
At about 3,100 m it is cold even in June, and nights are freezing in October. Dress modestly and in layers.
The border village of Mana is close by, with Vyas Gufa, Ganesh Gufa and Bheem Pul; the trek to Vasudhara falls starts here.
One common list adds Yogdhyan Badri (Pandukeshwar), Bhavishya Badri, Vridh Badri and Adi Badri to Badri Vishal — lists differ by tradition.

itinerary.h2: A sample three-day Badrinath yatra from Rishikesh
days: Drive up past Devprayag, Rudraprayag and Karnaprayag along the Alaknanda. Evening at Narsingh temple and rest early.
Drive on to Badrinath, bathe at Tapt Kund and take darshan. Afternoon at Mana — Vyas Gufa, Ganesh Gufa and Bheem Pul — and the evening aarti.
Early-morning darshan, visit Brahma Kapal, then drive down via Pandukeshwar towards Rudraprayag or Rishikesh.

What is the altitude of Badrinath?
About 3,100 m (Incredible India gives 3,133 m). It is cold even in June, so carry warm layers.
Per Incredible India, about 4:30 am to 1 pm and 4:30 pm to 9 pm. Hours can change in peak season and on festival days — confirm locally.
Is there a trek to Badrinath?
No. The road goes all the way to Badrinath town, and the temple is a short walk across the Alaknanda bridge.
How do I reach Badrinath by road?
From Rishikesh via Devprayag, Rudraprayag, Karnaprayag and Jyotirmath — about 298 km. The nearest airport is Dehradun and the railhead is Rishikesh.
Yes. Char Dham registration is compulsory and free on registrationandtouristcare.uk.gov.in, the Tourist Care Uttarakhand app or helpline 1364.
Where is Badrinath worshipped in winter?
At Yogdhyan Badri in Pandukeshwar (Uddhav and Kuber) and at Narsingh temple in Jyotirmath (Adi Shankaracharya's gaddi).
